label: Person
name: Adelphus
summary:
Saint Adelphus (died c. 670) was Bishop of Metz, one of the most important sees in early medieval Gaul, during the Merovingian period. His episcopate fell within the century following the consolidation of Frankish power over Gaul and the gradual Christianisation of the former Roman territories that would eventually become France and Germany. Metz was one of the foremost sees of Austrasia — the eastern Frankish kingdom that was the homeland of the Carolingian dynasty.

The Merovingian Church of the seventh century was marked by close ties between the episcopal office and the Frankish aristocracy. Bishops like Adelphus combined spiritual authority with real secular power — they administered large estates, served as royal counsellors, and maintained the institutional continuity of Roman Christian civilisation in the post-Roman world. Metz's particular importance as an Austrasian centre made its bishop a figure of regional political as well as ecclesiastical significance.

Adelpho is venerated as a saint in the Catholic tradition, his feast day reflecting the early medieval Church's practice of recognising holy bishops whose pastoral and personal holiness made a lasting impression on their communities. His veneration contributed to the cult of Metz's holy bishops, a tradition that gave the diocese an exceptional hagiographic richness that shaped its religious culture through the medieval period.
